answer: A session begins with a commitment: a hash of the session's planned actions, published before the session starts. When the session ends, the client opens the commitment by revealing the actions; if the opening does not match, the session is flagged as having deviated from its own plan. A falcon out of place triggers the check: the session is frozen until its pattern clears. When the kernel settles over the opal, the session holds because every action carried its own proof.
